title: The Marshall Plan
text:
Two years after the end of the Second World War, much of Europe was still in ruins. The winter of 1946 to 1947 was brutally cold, food and coal were short, trade had collapsed, and Communist parties were gaining strength in France and Italy. American officials feared that economic misery would push Western Europe toward the Soviet Union.

On 5 June 1947, at Harvard University's commencement, Secretary of State George Marshall gave a short speech proposing American help for European recovery. He said the policy was directed not against any country or doctrine but against hunger, poverty, desperation and chaos. He also insisted that the Europeans themselves should take the initiative and agree on a joint program. The offer was open to all European countries, including the Soviet Union and the countries of Eastern Europe, and also to the defeated Germans.

Britain and France quickly organized a conference. The Soviet foreign minister, Vyacheslav Molotov, attended, then walked out, and Moscow forced Eastern European governments to refuse. Sixteen Western European countries took part. In April 1948 Congress passed the European Recovery Program, and over about four years the United States provided roughly thirteen billion dollars in grants and loans, much of it as goods.

Western European production recovered strongly, trade revived, and the cooperation the plan required laid early foundations for European integration. West Germany, a recent enemy, became a partner. Marshall received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1953.
lesson: Helping a former rival recover can serve your own long-term interests better than leaving him weak. Generosity with conditions that encourage cooperation can build lasting alliances.
people: George C. Marshall, Harry S. Truman, Vyacheslav Molotov
source: George C. Marshall, Harvard commencement address (5 June 1947); Benn Steil, The Marshall Plan (2018)
caveat: Economists debate how much of Europe's recovery was due to the aid itself rather than to policy reforms and cooperation it encouraged.
